summary: Gone Forest Service cabin-with-firefinder lookout in Baker County; abandoned 1948; 1915 lightning fires reported from the station.

facts.design: Cabin with a fire finder on the roof
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1948; the register says the site is now gone.

events.note: A forester was named to take charge of the Bennett's Peak lookout station, where a new fire finder was to be located
Three lightning-caused forest fires reported within two days in August 1915
Newspaper item dated September 23, 1915: a fire reported from the lookout on East Eagle Creek, menacing valuable timber
Register says the cabin might have been replaced by a tower in 1932 (possibly; not confirmed)
Fred Groom, a lookout-dispatcher, went up on Bennett Peak on July 15

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cabin was built in the 1920s; firelookout.com says the 1910s. A 1914 newspaper item names a forester to take charge of the station, which fits the earlier date. The sources do not settle the build year.

sources.title: Bennett Peak Lookout Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites Register (Forest Fire Lookout Association)

notes_for_editor: Three sources. The brief's agency string reads U.S.Forest Service; corrected here to standard spacing. No height is recorded in any source. No source describes the site today, and access is not recorded. A web-search summary attributed the 1948 abandonment to an Idaho Bennett Mountain; the register and firelookout.com both state it for this site, so the search summary was not used.
